subject: NH2OH and hyponitrite (H2N2O2, 2 N) reconstructed from the Katsounaros thesis Diag 12.1 rates, their coverage of the N deficit of data/real/katsounaros2012_fig1_sn_naoh.json, the comparison with model B's hidden X, and the NH3 120-min question
summary: Every number tested reproduces with independent code: the rates are Origin-style finite differences (mean of the two adjacent interval slopes, one-sided at the ends), the inverse reproduces the thesis NO2-, N2 and N2O markers to 0.17/0.19/0.19 mM-N RMS against 11.43/1.89/0.73 for the trapezoid, the deficit and coverage table match the meta to 0.004 mM-N and 0.001, and model B's X peaks at 125.2 mM-N (25.0% of N) at 77.8 min and exceeds the unmeasured remainder by 15.0/62.7/35.5/29.2/13.1 mM-N at 60-180 min. The 2 N basis for hyponitrite is sound. Flags: (1) the X-minus-remainder excess mixes model B's misfit of the observed species with the hidden-pool size (at 90 min X exceeds the whole deficit by 26.8 mM-N); (2) the 60- and 180-min excesses (15 and 13 mM-N) are smaller than the deficit uncertainty if the +-10% bars are 1 sigma (20-32 mM-N); (3) the NH3 rates are inconsistent with the thesis Diag 12.3 NH3 markers (forward residual up to 0.144 mM/min, 78 px), so the rates were computed from liquid-phase data that differ from the plotted figure for at least NH3; (4) this new evidence weakens the earlier 'Daniel misclicked NH3 at 120 min' verdict, which should be treated as unresolved until the journal figure is checked. No values in the dataset were changed.
method: Own scripts in literature/extraction_scripts/k12_verify/ (v1_fd_scheme.py, v1b_endcheck_power.py, v2_coverage.py, v3_modelB_X.py, v6_nh3.py); the analyst's literature/extraction_scripts/k12_hidden/ scripts were not read or run. Inputs: data/digitized_inputs/katsounaros2009thesis_diag12p1_rates/extracted.csv (stored rates), data/digitized_inputs/katsounaros2009thesis_diag12p3_xcheck/extracted.csv (thesis markers, kind = data), data/real/katsounaros2012_fig1_sn_naoh.json (Daniel), worlds/W3_katsounaros_hidden_intermediate.json with the repo simulator (nernstwork.simulate, run with PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python). Thesis text layer (reader pages = printed + 30; session scratch, not retained) read for printed pp. 70-71, 138-145, 184-192 and 201.

checks.name: claim1_forward_differentiation_NO2
checks.detail: Differentiating the thesis Diag 12.3 NO2- markers (0, 107.44, 132.21, 99.01, 38.74, 10.81, 6.29 mM) with the mean of the two adjacent interval slopes and one-sided end slopes gives the stored Diag 12.1 rates to 0.0019, 0.0011, 0.0005, 0.0016, -0.0010, 0.0035, -0.0096 mM/min (max 0.0096, 0.0035 without the 180-min end point). Daniel's NO2- values give max 0.0091. numpy.gradient with second-order ends misses by 1.38 mM/min at t = 0 and 0.38 at 180 min, so the end treatment is one-sided first order, as in Origin's Differentiate. The verified rate reading error is 0.0039 (top panel).

checks.name: claim1_inverse_vs_thesis_markers
checks.detail: Own recursive inverse (s0 = g0, s_i = 2 g_i - s_(i-1), c0 = 0), RMS against the thesis Diag 12.3 markers at 30-180 min in mM-N: fd_inverse NO2 0.17, N2 0.19, N2O 0.19, NH3 2.62; trapezoid 11.43, 1.89, 0.73, 2.97; left step 59.6, 13.58, 3.05; right step 63.99, 12.30, 2.45. Against Daniel: fd_inverse 0.32, 0.66, 0.47, 1.02. All match the meta's scheme_validation tables. Trapezoid NO2- at 30 min is 86.73 against 107.44 (20.7 mM low). On the non-uniform gas grid (0, 4, 15, 30, ... min) the mean-of-slopes form fits better than (c[i+1]-c[i-1])/(t[i+1]-t[i-1]) (least-squares inverse, N2 0.19 vs 0.73, N2O 0.19 vs 0.46 mM-N RMS), which supports Origin's specific algorithm. Limits: for NO2- the inverse check is not independent of the forward check; N2 and N2O are checked only at the 30-min points, the 15-min concentrations are not plotted.

checks.name: claim1_scheme_applies_to_NH2OH_and_H2N2O2
checks.detail: On the 30-min grid the inverse splits into two chains: c30 = 30 g0, c90 = c30 + 60 g60, c150 = c90 + 60 g120 (anchored by the half-hidden t = 0 rate marker) and c60 = 60 g30, c120 = c60 + 60 g90, c180 = c120 + 60 g150 (anchored by c0 = 0). The unused last equation is a cross-chain check. Residuals: NH2OH -0.0018, H2N2O2 0.0011 mM/min (bottom-panel reading error 0.0028), and both chains settle at the same late level (NH2OH -0.01 and 0.04 mM; H2N2O2 41.15 and 40.13 mM-N). A synthetic test (v1b_endcheck_power.py) shows that exact instantaneous derivatives of a sharp peak, fed to the same inverse, give an end-check residual of 2.6 mM/min and +-19-60 mM sawtooth errors, so the near-zero NH2OH checks favour the finite-difference reading for NH2OH, where the scheme matters (27.0 vs 16.9 mM at 60 min, fd_inverse vs trapezoid). For a slowly varying hyponitrite-like sigmoid the test is weak (residual -0.014), but there the schemes differ by only 1.0-2.5 mM-N. Reading-error propagation (Monte Carlo, worst verified errors): fd_inverse sd 0.08-0.29 mM for NH2OH and 0.17-0.58 mM-N for 2 x H2N2O2.

checks.name: claim2_deficit_and_coverage
checks.detail: Deficit = 500 - (NO3 + NO2 + N2 + N2O + NH3) from Daniel's dataset: 114.29, 142.19, 95.68, 106.31, 86.38, 77.74 mM-N (22.9, 28.4, 19.1, 21.3, 17.3, 15.5% of N) at 30-180 min, max difference from the meta 0.004. fd_inverse NH2OH 7.72, 27.02, 5.69, 2.29, -0.01, 0.04; 2 x H2N2O2 3.58, 12.37, 30.23, 38.08, 41.15, 40.13; coverage 0.099, 0.277, 0.375, 0.380, 0.476, 0.517 (identical); 68% intervals with the 3.43 mM-N deficit sigma identical within 0.001; trapezoid and step-rule coverages identical. Unmeasured remainder 102.99, 102.80, 59.76, 65.94, 45.24, 37.57 mM-N (20.6, 20.6, 12.0, 13.2, 9.0, 7.5% of N). Deficit-weighted unmeasured share 0.665 (x2) and 0.798 (x1). With the thesis-marker deficit (113.69, 146.11, 93.12, 99.29, 83.87, 80.60): coverage 0.099, 0.270, 0.386, 0.407, 0.491, 0.498 (meta 0.406 at 120 min, rounding). The remainder at 30-60 min ranges 98.8-111.2 mM-N across integration schemes and deficit sources, so 'peaks at about 103 at 30-60 min' holds to about +-8. If the +-10% bars are 1 sigma, the deficit sigma is 27.6, 20.0, 21.8, 26.3, 30.2, 31.9 mM-N and the coverage 68% ranges are 0.080-0.131, 0.243-0.322, 0.306-0.484, 0.305-0.503, 0.354-0.732, 0.363-0.845 (meta matches).

checks.name: claim4_H2N2O2_counted_as_2N
checks.detail: In the same Diag 12.1 the 2-N gases are plotted per molecule: the fd_inverse N2 x 2 matches the N-equivalent Diag 12.3 markers to 0.19 mM-N RMS, while x 1 would give 154.8 mM at 180 min against 309.3. Diag 12.3 is N-equivalent (the thesis model eqs 12.23-12.28 conserve N 1:1; per molecule the 180-min sum would exceed 500). Hyponitrite was measured by ion chromatography (printed pp. 70-71: AS19, 20 mM NaOH, 1 mL/min, 248 nm, linear 0.4-100 mg/L, LOD 50 ug/L, RSD 5% for 9 repeats). The calibration curve (Diag 5.5) is in mg/L of N2O2^2-; the body text gives the standard as 10 mg/L Na2N2O2 while the Diag 5.4 caption gives 10 mg/L N2O2^2-. Either way it is a mass concentration of one molecular species, which converts to molecules, not N-equivalents. The thesis also writes hyponitrite per molecule (2 HNO -> H2N2O2, eq. 12.10; H2N2O2 -> N2O + H2O, eq. 12.11; a 0.05 M Na2N2O2 electrolysis, p. 189). Mass balance does not decide the basis: x1 coverage would be 0.083, 0.234, 0.217, 0.201, 0.238, 0.259, which is also feasible. So the 2 N basis rests on consistency and convention, not on an explicit statement for Diag 12.1, and that is the right default.

checks.name: claim6_NH3_120_and_the_misclick_verdict
checks.detail: Thesis copy: the NH3 open triangle at 120 min sits at about 26 mM. My own reads on p221.jpg (own calibration, 0.598168 mM/px): bar midpoint 25.76-25.91 mM (lower cap row 2798.0 = 23.22 mM; the upper cap shares a 4-row grey band with the NO3 lower cap); bar-midpoint-to-base offset of the clean 180-min triangle (-8.18 px) applied to the 120-min base gives 25.91 mM. The triangle's base stroke is at 21.01 mM, and Daniel's 19.60 maps to row 2804.05, 2.4 px below the base on the error-bar stem. So 19.6 is not a reading of the thesis copy. But the thesis's own Diag 12.1 NH3 rates contradict its Diag 12.3 markers: the forward check against the thesis markers misses by 0.034, -0.054, -0.014, 0.144, 0.004, -0.086, -0.000 mM/min (18, 29, 8, 78, 2, 47, 0 px; reading error 0.0028 = 1.5 px), whereas NO2- from the same liquid samples matches to 0.0035. Inverting the NH3 rates gives 3.28, 8.00, 14.85, 20.80, 23.85, 27.13 mM (sd 0.1-0.3), against thesis markers 4.31, 4.79, 15.03, 26.23, 24.27, 27.38 (differences -1.0, +3.2, -0.2, -5.4, -0.4, -0.3) and Daniel 4.98, 7.64, 13.62, 19.60, 23.59, 27.58 (differences -1.7, +0.4, +1.2, +1.2, +0.3, -0.5). The two points where Daniel departs from the thesis copy (60 and 120 min) are the only two where the rates also depart from it, and both depart in Daniel's direction. Replacing only those two thesis values with Daniel's cuts the worst forward residual from 0.144 to 0.034 mM/min. So the earlier explanations (occlusion bias at 60 min; misclick at 120 min) are no longer the most likely ones. They now compete with the hypothesis that the journal Fig. 1, which is a re-plot (its curves are model B, not the thesis constants), plots NH3 near 8 and 20 mM at 60 and 120 min, consistent with the data behind the thesis rates. The thesis-copy features also lie near the rate-implied values (visible-part midpoint 7.3 at 60 min, triangle base 21.0 at 120 min), so the two hypotheses cannot be separated without the journal image. Recommendation: do not replace Daniel's NH3 values with the thesis-copy 4.8/26.2; flag NH3 at 60 and 120 min as source-dependent (+-3 and +-6 mM); check the journal PDF Fig. 1 at pixel level. Effect here: the 120-min deficit changes by 6.6 mM-N and the coverage moves from 0.380 to 0.406.

claims_tested.result: confirmed (0.17/0.19/0.19 vs 11.43/1.89/0.73; forward NO2- residual <= 0.0096 mM/min)
confirmed (max differences 0.004 mM-N and 0.000 in coverage)

claims_tested.claim: model B X peaks ~125 mM-N at ~78 min and exceeds the remainder by 15/63/35/29/13 mM-N at 60-180 min
claims_tested.result: confirmed (125.16 at 77.8 min; 15.03/62.72/35.50/29.16/13.08); see issues for interpretation

claims_tested.claim: H2N2O2 counted as 2 N per molecule
claims_tested.result: sound (consistent with the per-molecule gases in the same figure, IC mass-based calibration, per-molecule chemistry; not stated explicitly)

claims_tested.claim: NH3 rates invert to ~20.8 mM at 120 min (Daniel 19.6) while thesis marker and bar midpoint give ~26
claims_tested.result: confirmed (20.80 +- 0.24; marker/bar midpoint 25.8-25.9); the misclick verdict should be downgraded to unresolved

issues: Interpretation of X vs remainder: X(t) minus deficit(t) equals the summed observed data minus model B's summed observed species, so the excess of X over the unmeasured remainder includes model B's misfit, not only the hidden-pool size. At 90 min X (122.5) exceeds even the whole deficit (95.7) by 26.8 mM-N because model B under-predicts NO3 + NO2 there (149.3 vs 184.1 mM-N). The 62.7 mM-N excess at 90 min is 26.8 of misfit plus 35.9 of measured intermediates. The README's 'X is too large mid-run and peaks too late' should say this.

Uncertainty next to the excess: if the +-10% bars are 1 sigma, the deficit carries 20-32 mM-N (and the remainder at least as much), so the 60- and 180-min excesses (15.0 and 13.1 mM-N) are within 1 sigma. Only the 90-min (62.7) and, marginally, the 120-min (35.5) excesses exceed it. The README lists the excesses without this caveat.

Wording: 'lower the required unobserved pool from model B's 25% of N to about 21%' compares model B's X peak with the data. The data-implied unobserved pool drops from the 28.4% deficit (60 min) to 20.6% once the measured intermediates are removed; model B's X peaks at 25.0%.
Wording: 'Hyponitrite holds nearly all of it' from 90 min. At 90 min NH2OH is 5.7 of 35.9 mM-N (16%); 'nearly all' (>= 94%) holds from 120 min.

NH3 rates vs thesis markers (already flagged by the analyst): the forward residual reaches 0.144 mM/min (78 px, about 50 times the reading error), so the liquid-phase data behind Diag 12.1 are not the plotted Diag 12.3 values for NH3. The fd_inverse NH2OH and H2N2O2 are the concentrations implied by the rates as plotted; whether they equal the measured concentrations cannot be checked, because neither species is plotted as a concentration.

Earlier verdict to revisit (not edited here): data/digitized_inputs/tin_xcheck_verification.json check A2 ranks 'a click on the base/stem of a crowded cluster' as the most likely cause of Daniel's NH3 = 19.6 at 120 min, and katsounaros2009thesis_diag12p3_xcheck/comparison_vs_daniel.json says it 'looks like a click on the wrong object'. Both are hedged ('unless the paper image differs'), but with the rate inversion the paper-differs branch is at least as likely. The same applies to the occlusion explanation for NH3 at 60 min (Daniel 7.64; rates 8.00; thesis marker 4.79). Neither file should be used to correct data/real until the journal figure is pixel-checked.

Pre-existing documentation discrepancy, not in this dataset: docs/SPEC.md section 7b says model B's X 'peaks at 122 mM-N (24%) around 85 min', and the W3 reference notes say 'about 24%'. The simulator gives 125.2 mM-N (25.0%) at 77.8 min. 122.5 is the value at the 90-min sample.
